descriptors.definition: The objective is to prescribe the accounting treatment and disclosure requirements for property held to earn rentals or for capital appreciation. It establishes the cost model framework for measuring such properties.
inclusion: land held for rentals or capital appreciation
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from general asset standards by specifically focusing on rental-generating or appreciation-driven real estate.

descriptors.definition: The standard applies to the recognition, measurement, and disclosure of investment property. It explicitly excludes biological assets tied to agricultural activity and mineral reserves.
inclusion: properties held by owners or lessees as right-of-use assets for rental or appreciation
exclusion: non-regenerative resources like oil and gas
nearby_distinctions: Excludes operating properties covered under agricultural or extractive industry standards.

descriptors.definition: Provides core accounting terminology including investment property, owner-occupied property, fair value, cost, and carrying amount. These definitions govern the classification and valuation rules across financial statements.
inclusion: properties held to earn rental income
exclusion: properties used in production or administrative functions
properties held for sale in ordinary course
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between investment properties generating independent cash flows and owner-occupied assets dependent on broader entity operations.

descriptors.concept_name: Classification Of Property As Investment Property Or Owner-Occupied Property
descriptors.definition: Classification depends on whether the property is held for rental or capital appreciation rather than operational use or ordinary sale. Investment properties generate cash flows largely independent of other assets.
inclusion: land held for long-term capital appreciation
vacant buildings held to be leased out
exclusion: properties intended for sale in ordinary course of business
nearby_distinctions: Separates investment assets generating independent cash flows from owner-occupied assets requiring operational support.

descriptors.definition: An investment property is recognized when future economic benefits are probable and its cost can be measured reliably. Subsequent day-to-day servicing costs are expensed, while qualifying replacement parts are capitalized and replaced parts derecognized.
exclusion: routine repairs and maintenance labor costs
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between capitalizable structural replacements and expensed routine maintenance.

descriptors.definition: Purchased investment properties are initially measured at cost, including transaction costs and directly attributable expenditures. Start-up costs, abnormal waste, and pre-occupancy operating losses are excluded from initial cost.
nearby_distinctions: Separates necessary acquisition overheads from abnormal development inefficiencies and general operational losses.

descriptors.definition: Entities must adopt the cost model as their accounting policy for all investment properties subsequent to initial recognition. Fair value must still be measured and disclosed for informational purposes even when applying the cost model.
inclusion: cost-based carrying amounts adjusted for depreciation and impairment
exclusion: carrying value adjustments via upward revaluations into profit or loss under the cost model
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts the mandatory cost model for balance sheet recognition with the mandatory fair value disclosure requirement.

descriptors.definition: Property transfers to or from investment property occur only when there is an actual change in use supported by evidence. A mere change in management intention does not constitute a change in use and does not alter the carrying amount.
inclusion: inception of an operating lease to another party
exclusion: changes in management intent without physical or operational alterations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between substantive operational changes requiring reclassification and subjective intent shifts that do not.

descriptors.definition: Investment properties are derecognized upon disposal or permanent withdrawal when no future economic benefits are expected. Gains or losses are determined as the difference between net disposal proceeds and the carrying amount, recognized in profit or loss.
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates permanent derecognition due to retirement or sale from temporary idle holding status.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose their measurement accounting policy, criteria for distinguishing investment properties, rental income amounts, and direct operating expenses. Comprehensive reconciliations of carrying amounts from beginning to end of the period are also required.
inclusion: rental income amounts recognized in profit or loss
gross carrying amount and accumulated depreciation reconciliations
exclusion: omission of fair value disclosures when cost model is adopted
nearby_distinctions: Complements general lease disclosures with property-specific operating and reconciliation disclosures.

descriptors.concept_name: Extracts Of Financial Statements Of Listed Entity
descriptors.definition: Provides practical illustrations of financial statement presentation and accounting policy disclosures for investment properties using corporate reporting examples. These extracts demonstrate the application of reporting standards in corporate practice.
inclusion: published financial statement disclosures from listed infrastructure entities
nearby_distinctions: Provides empirical presentation examples distinct from theoretical standard definitions.
